message.content:
Nxeon platform: implement the QUICK FIXES from the signup-friction report plus much richer first-party activity and payment logging. Repo /opt/nxeon (NEVER edit/build/install inside /opt/nxeon; worktree: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/nxeon-wt-signupfix -b feature/signup-fixes-activity main`; if you need `prisma generate` use a separate node_modules copy in the worktree, never symlinked to prod; read /root/.claude/projects/-root/memory/nxeon-worktree-nodemodules-hazard.md (NEVER `git add -A`), nxeon-brand-voice-no-provider.md, nxeon-deploy-winback.md, nxeon-checkout-conversion-research.md, nxeon-visitor-device-analytics.md, nxeon-marketing-v1-port.md (live marketing pages are generated by tools/nxm)). READ /root/agent-notes/signup-friction/REPORT.md in full first. Do NOT deploy or merge; prod DB SELECT-only; never send any email/notification; no pkill by pattern; never disable the sandbox. RESOURCE RULE (host crashed today from agent memory use): no `next build` / full test suite unless `free -g` shows >= 12 GB available; tsc/tests with `nice -n 19 ionice -c3` and `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072`; targeted tests; stop dev servers right after use (kill by own PID).

COORDINATION: another agent is building an admin Reports page (branch feature/admin-reports, worktree /tank/nxeon-wt-reports) that will read customer journeys and may add an ErrorEvent table. Put all new event capture behind ONE small module (e.g. lib/activity-events.ts with a typed event catalogue and a `recordActivity()` function) and one additive table, so that agent can consume it; describe the schema clearly in your final report. Don't edit their worktree.

OWNER'S INSTRUCTIONS:
A) "Do the quick fixes from the signup report."
B) "I don't want to flat-out tell people they are unavailable. I feel like the custom servers are deterring people. We need to portray ourselves as a large hosting provider with no limits."
C) "I want those payment records logged. Even when I check a customer's account I don't see very many recorded actions. I want more detailed actions and page visits, even the steps on the deploy wizard they are on or made it to."

BUILD:
1. Quick fixes from the report:
   - Free-intent landing pages (/free-vps, /free-minecraft; via the generators): fix the title/meta/hero so they're honest and match what we actually offer (free Minecraft exists; free VPS does not), and give a clear, attractive next step (e.g. cheapest VPS / free Minecraft) instead of a dead end. No fabricated claims.
   - Stale provisioning state: find why two Oct 2 servers (an 8 GB Valheim and an 8 GB Project Zomboid) still show 'large download' as their step text days after RUNNING and never got a ready email; fix the code path; list (don't run) the exact data repair SQL for those rows and note that sending their ready email needs the owner's approval.
   - 'Failed to find Server Action' after deploys: a global handler that detects a stale client after a deploy and shows a friendly 'A new version is available, refresh' prompt (and auto-retry where safe), plus whatever caused the /dashboard/support 500s on Oct 4 and /api/chat/upload 500s on Oct 1 if still reproducible from code/logs.
   - Hosting wizard: validate the domain at the domain step, not at Payment.
   - Unverified-email nudge in the dashboard (no email sending; in-app banner only).
2. Capacity messaging (owner instruction B): customers should never see 'sold out' / 'unavailable' / 'limited' for a region or a size. Read lib/region-placement.ts, lib/node-capacity.ts (scheduleNode/regionAvailability, strict region-bound placement), the RAM guard, and the deploy wizard + custom builder UI. Implement: the order is always accepted in the region the customer chose; when no node has room right now, the order goes into a 'queued for setup' state with honest, positive copy ('Your server is being prepared, we'll email you when it's ready' with the expected wait, never 'unavailable'), an URGENT admin alert names the region/size/customer so staff can add capacity, and the user id is logged with every RAM-guard refusal. Do not oversell a node past the hard RAM guard (never risk OOM-killing customers); queueing is the safety valve. Make the custom server builder feel like a normal premium option, not a 'contact sales / enterprise / big-ask' detour (review its entry point copy in the wizard 'Running a community, enterprise or commercial server?' card and the custom flow) so large sizes read as routine. Remove any copy that implies small scale or limits.
3. Payment logging (C): record every payment event with customer, amount, currency, method, country, and outcome: checkout opened, checkout cancelled/expired, payment succeeded, failed (decline code, 3DS required/failed, insufficient funds etc. from Stripe), refunds, disputes, PayPal equivalents, local payment methods (PayNow, GrabPay, UPI...), wallet top-ups, renewals (sweep, saved card, admin Renew now), dunning steps. Add the Stripe webhook events needed (payment_intent.payment_failed, checkout.session.expired, charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created, etc.; check which the endpoint already subscribes to and list exactly which events the owner must enable in the Stripe dashboard). Also check that local payment methods actually appear for India, Indonesia, Singapore and Bangladesh in checkout, and report.
4. Activity tracking (C): page visits for signed-in users (route, referrer, time on page roughly, device), every deploy-wizard step reached and every field change that matters (product, game, plan, region, OS, add-ons, coupon), abandonment point, errors shown to the user, key dashboard actions (start/stop/restart, console opened, files used, mods installed, settings changed, tickets/chats, billing actions), auth events (signup, login, verify, password reset). Respect privacy: no passwords, no file contents, no keystrokes, no card data, no content of customer servers; first-party only; rate-limited and batched client beacon; retention setting (default 180 days) with a prune job; IPs truncated in storage if feasible. Update the privacy policy page copy accordingly (list what's collected) and flag it for owner review.
5. Admin: on the customer's admin account page, a clear Activity timeline (filterable: pages, wizard, payments, actions, errors, auth) with the payment records, and a per-customer 'deploy wizard progress' summary (furthest step, last configuration, where they dropped). Keep existing audit log entries integrated.
6. Tests for pure logic + webhook handlers (signature verification, idempotency), tsc clean, targeted tests. Screenshots under /root/agent-notes/signup-fixes/. Append docs/DOCUMENTATION.md. Commit explicit paths; messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Final report: branch+commits, each fix, the event schema + catalogue, Stripe events the owner must enable, data repair SQL for approval, privacy-policy changes for review, deploy steps.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector — starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one — instead of publishing a page, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. Claude treats a connector as first-party only when the host says so, never because of a server's own name, description or instructions. Claude publishes an artifact for apps, sites, dashboards and games, and whenever the person asks for an artifact or for an HTML or Markdown page to view or share. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it. Advice that the person will act on by themselves, right away, in the code they are working on is not meant for other people, so Claude does not need to publish it.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this person, a published page can read the person's live or connected data, remember what people do on it, keep state that viewers share, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question, store files people add, or give the viewer a file to save. A page declares these through the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of this would make the page more useful, Claude must load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code.** Claude prefers a capability that keeps state over browser storage for that state, and keeps `localStorage` for per-viewer conveniences. Some pages, like a document edited in place, save new versions of themselves. Such a save reaches this session like any other republish, as a notice on a watched artifact or a conflict on Claude's next publish, and Claude then re-reads the page, merges the changes and republishes.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Claude always authors the page as `.html`, and publishes a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly asks for one. When the person shares a Markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, Claude builds an HTML page from its content, keeping its substance and designing the page as it would any other artifact rather than transcribing the Markdown one to one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB work, but each artifact has its own origin and what a page stores lives only in that viewer's browser. It survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices or Claude. It can come back empty, or the accessor can throw, in a private window, with cleared or blocked site data, in previews or during thumbnail capture, so Claude wraps every read and write in try/catch and makes the page render correctly without it. Claude uses it only for per-viewer conveniences, such as a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section or an unsent draft, and never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers or be read back by Claude. That state belongs in a runtime capability.

**Size**: Claude keeps the rendered page at 16MB or smaller, and embedded `data:` URIs count toward that limit.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data, images, or further HTML pages) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. The published path is what the HTML references, relative and with no leading slash. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

content.content:
1	# Signup journey and friction, last 7 days (2026-09-29 to 10-06) vs previous 7 and previous 30
2	
3	Read-only analysis (prod DB SELECT, journalctl, nginx, code). Internal QA accounts (nxeon-internal.test, nxeon.local) excluded
4	from rates; one QA account generated 35 of the 49 game provision errors and 79 of 93 game "complete" events this week.
5	No customer-identifying data is written here. Cohort = CUSTOMER accounts created in the window.
6	
7	## Summary
8	
9	Signups rose 56 percent week over week (150 real vs 96; previous-30-day average is 21/day, this week 21.6/day, last week 13.7/day).
10	The growth is almost entirely cold, free-intent traffic: 60 percent of this week's signups were ChatGPT-attributed
11	(utm_source=chatgpt.com, vs 26 percent last week), 58 landed first on /free-vps and 28 on /free-minecraft, and 45 percent are
12	Mobile (Android 41 percent), up from 33 percent. Those segments almost never buy: the 83 signups from /free-vps over two weeks
13	produced 0 servers and 0 paid top-ups; the 28 from /free-minecraft produced 0 and 0; mobile signups this week produced 0 servers
14	and 0 paid top-ups from 68 (1 server from 32 the week before). Because of that mix, the signup-to-order rate looks worse this week
15	(9 percent have a server vs 7 percent, but wizard-open fell to 56 percent from 69 percent and "reached Payment" fell to 23 percent
16	from 44 percent), even though the product itself (provisioning, wizard) is working: 23 of 23 new-user servers are RUNNING, the median
17	order-to-"deployed email" time is about 4.5 minutes, and card/Stripe top-ups are succeeding. The money friction is therefore
18	(1) acquisition-promise mismatch ("free VPS" pages vs no free VPS), (2) mobile wizard drop, (3) Payment-step abandonment, concentrated
19	in India/Indonesia/Singapore/Bangladesh, with no instrumentation to see why, and (4) post-signup activation (free Minecraft servers that
20	nobody connects to). Nothing in the Oct 5-6 deploys shows up as a new customer-facing regression; the 15:23 UTC crash cost about 5 minutes
21	and 29 /login 502s.
22	
23	## Funnel (real accounts, users)
24	
25	| Stage | Prev 30d (14-44d ago) | Prev 7d | This 7d |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| Signups | 627 (20.9/day) | 96 | 150 |
28	| Google sign-in share | 70% | 76% | 79% |
29	| Email signups verified (of email signups) | n/a | 16 of 23 (70%) | 23 of 31 (74%) |
30	| Opened any deploy wizard | 507 (81%) | 66 (69%) | 84 (56%) |
31	|  of which VPS / game / hosting / email | | 36/37/10/3 | 47/45/3/5 |
32	| Reached the Payment step | 133 (21%) | 42 (44%) | 34 (23%) |
33	| Has any server (incl. admin-granted/free) | 24 (3.8%) | 7 (7.3%) | 14 (9.3%) |
34	| Real paid top-up (Stripe or PayPal) | 26 (4.1%) | 9 (9.4%) | 9 (6.0%) |
35	| Returned 1+ day after signup | n/a | 15 (16%) | 23 (15%) |
36	| Returned 1+ day, owners of a server | | 4 of 7 | 9 of 14 (64%) |
37	| Returned 1+ day, non-owners | | 11 of 89 (12%) | 14 of 136 (10%) |
38	
39	Session-level wizard steps (all visitors, QA excluded, steps used since the Sep 14 wizard rewrite):
40	
41	| Wizard | Step | Prev 7d | This 7d |
42	|---|---|---|---|
43	| VPS | Configure | 60 | 59 |
44	|  | Region | 45 | 29 |
45	|  | Payment | 44 | 27 |
46	|  | Completed (events) | 5 | 2 |
47	| Game | Game | 50 | 48 |
48	|  | Server (plan) | 43 | 49 |
49	|  | Region | 26 | 22 |
50	|  | Payment | 24 | 19 |
51	|  | Completed (events) | 7 | 14 (about 11 users) |
52	
53	Cohort mix, this week vs last: ChatGPT 91 vs 25 signups; Google organic 24 vs 39; direct 13 vs 5. Desktop 72 vs 58; Mobile 68 vs 32.
54	Top countries this week: India 16, Brazil 9, Germany 9, US 9, Indonesia 8, Philippines 5, Bangladesh 5, Vietnam 5, Mexico 5, Pakistan 5.
55	Brazil and Mexico are new in the top list (last week they were not in the top 10). Self-reported source ("heard about us", 150 users): ChatGPT 37, Google 12,
56	YouTube 5, 80 skipped. Partner program: referral clicks 101 this week vs 8 last week, 7 converted to a signup, 8 PartnerCustomer rows.
57	
58	By segment (this week + last, real accounts):
59	
60	| Segment | Signups | Opened wizard | Reached Payment | Has server | Paid |
61	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
62	| Desktop | 130 | 86 | 52 | 19 | 16 |
63	| Mobile | 100 | 57 | 22 | 1 | 2 |
64	| Landed on /free-vps | 83 | 53 | 21 | 0 | 0 |
65	| Landed on /free-minecraft (this week only) | 28 | 8 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
66	| ChatGPT-attributed, this week | 91 | 51 | 19 | 7 | 6 |
67	| ChatGPT-attributed, last week | 25 | 20 | 15 | 1 | 1 |
68	| Google organic (this week + last) | 63 | 41 | 23 | 5 | 4 |
69	
70	## Top friction points (ranked)
71	
72	### 1. Free-intent landing pages bring signups that cannot convert (project, but the copy change is quick)
73	- 83 /free-vps signups in 14 days, 0 servers, 0 paid. 28 /free-minecraft signups this week, 0 servers, 0 paid.
74	- The page itself says "nobody gives a real VPS away; there is no free tier" but the title/H1/URL ("Free VPS", "Start free") pull in people searching for a free VPS. Page title: "Free VPS: start free, no credit card". The sign-up credit is 0 for all 150 new users (signupCreditCents is 0), so "claim any free-credit offer" has nothing behind it.
75	- Fix: (quick) change the /free-vps hero to state what is actually free (free Minecraft server, no card to sign up) and show the price of the cheapest paid server in the hero; add a first-visit "starter credit" if the owner wants this traffic to convert; track /free-vps visitors separately in the admin dashboard so these signups do not mask real conversion. (project) decide whether ChatGPT-sourced "free" queries are the audience to chase; they generate signups but not revenue, which is consistent with the earlier finding that conversion (not traffic) is the bottleneck.
76	
77	### 2. Mobile signups never reach a server (project)
78	- 68 mobile signups this week: 35 opened a wizard, 10 reached Payment, 0 ordered, 0 paid (week before: 32, 22, 12, 1, 2).
79	- Game wizard on mobile: 25 users hit step 1, 18 hit Server, only 5 reach Region and 5 Payment; desktop is 49, 48, 25, 24. So game wizard loses mobile users between Server (plan) and Region (28 percent proceed vs 52 percent on desktop). VPS: Configure 34 mobile to Region 18.
80	- Android is 62 of 150 signups (Mobile Chrome 54); iOS is only 9.
81	- Fix: audit /dashboard/deploy on a 390 px Android viewport (plan cards, region step, sticky continue button, keyboard covering the CTA, long single-column scroll); consider a "continue on desktop" link or email-me-this-config at the Payment step. Add a mobile/desktop split to /admin/deploy-funnel. Project (1-2 days).
82	
83	### 3. Payment step abandonment with no visibility into why (quick instrumentation, then fix)
84	- 34 users reached Payment this week; 9 paid (26 percent). Last week 42 and 9 (21 percent), prior 30 days 133 and 26.
85	- Reached-Payment-to-paid by country (two weeks): India 7 reached, 1 paid; Indonesia 5 and 0; Singapore 6 and 0; Bangladesh 3 and 0; Iran 2 and 0; Netherlands 2 and 0; vs Philippines 3 of 7 and Vietnam 3 of 5, Malaysia 2 of 2, Australia 2 of 2.
86	- The data cannot say why. Payment goes through hosted Stripe Checkout and PayPal; the app logs nothing for card declines, 3DS failures, abandoned Checkout sessions or currency problems, and DeployFunnelEvent has no "checkout opened", "checkout cancelled", or "payment failed" event type (only 3 hosting "ORDER_ERROR"s and one VPS "impersonating" error appear at the Payment step). Web logs show only one Stripe error pattern, "[cards] detach failed ... not attached to a customer" (7 occurrences), and 2 "PaymentMethod previously used without Customer" transient billing errors on a renewal. PayPal: 3 PENDING gameOrder and 3 PENDING order that never completed in Sept 20-30 plus one "account not vault-enabled" fallback warning per restart.
87	- Fix: (quick) add events checkout_opened / checkout_cancelled / checkout_return(success) and a Stripe webhook handler that writes payment_intent.payment_failed with decline_code and country into DeployFunnelEvent or ErrorLog; (quick) confirm the local-methods endpoint (UPI, GrabPay, FPX, etc.) is surfaced for India/Indonesia/Singapore/Bangladesh at the Payment step; (project) wallet-minimum / first-month price display in local currency for the emerging markets that make up 50 to 60 percent of signups.
88	
89	### 4. Free Minecraft activation gap (quick to investigate, medium to fix)
90	- 40 free Minecraft servers were created by new users in 14 days (33 this week; median 1.9 minutes after signup, so the create flow is fast). Only 6 of 40 (15 percent) were ever woken by a player, only 1 reached real multiplayer. Upsell was shown 22 times, clicked 4, and 1 of the 40 owners later bought a paid server.
91	- Chat topics from new users: "How do I invite my Bedrock player", "how to make it bedrock", "My Minecraft server is offline ... The VM must be running to control the game service" (Oct 4), "From where I can manage my server", "I cant connect to my server" (ticket). Sign that "how to connect and invite a friend" is the first-hour question.
92	- Fix: after create, show connect address (Java and Bedrock), copy button, "send to a friend" share link, and a "waiting for first player" state; add the first-wake nudge email at +30 min if nobody has connected. Quick win with a high effect on the 21 percent of new users who take this path.
93	
94	### 5. Game-port verification failures and stale provisioning state (Bedrock fix shipped; verify)
95	- Real customers' game provisions failed with "game port N never opened ... ECONNREFUSED after ~307 s" 12 times in 14 days (Minecraft 25565 x2, Valheim 2456 x4 on node 178.63.94.114, CS-style 27015 x2, and Bedrock 19132/udp x3 on Oct 6 04:00-05:31 UTC across two nodes, before the 05:24 Bedrock TRANSPORT=raknet commit reached prod at 05:34 and a customer retried). Failure emails (`server_provision_failed`) went to 3 new users on Oct 1 (38 mails, most for QA servers) and 2 on Oct 2.
96	- None of the new-user servers is in ERROR; all 23 are RUNNING and order-to-deployed email is 2 to 10 minutes except Rust 4 GB (24.5 min) and Left 4 Dead 2 (29.5 min).
97	- Two new-user servers (Valheim 8 GB and Project Zomboid 8 GB, both Oct 2) show status RUNNING but provisioningStep still reads "Installing the game, this one is a large download..." 4.6 days later and no `server_deployed` email ever sent: the customer is never told the game is ready, and the step text is stale. Quick fix: clear provisioningStep on first successful A2S/port check and send the deployed email; add a watchdog for RUNNING servers with a non-empty provisioningStep older than 30 minutes.
98	- Fix: verify the Bedrock fix with a real Bedrock order on staging; alert when a real customer sees a PROVISION_FAILED event (currently only visible in the funnel table).
99	
100	### 6. Capacity refusals for large VPS configs (quick to confirm, project to fix)
101	- ErrorLog and web logs: "RAM guard refused node-5, node-2, node-4 for a 32768 MB VM" 96 times Oct 2-6; "...node-5, node-2, node-4, node-6 for a 52224 MB VM" 7 times on Oct 6 (so node-6 is enabled but still full or ineligible for that size); "node-2, node-4 for a 16384 MB VM" 26; "node-4 for a 4096 MB VM" 43 (Oct 1 to Oct 6, including 14 on Oct 6). These errors carry no userId, so I cannot confirm they are customers. One new customer's Custom 6 vCPU / 32 GB VPS was finally created at 14:01 UTC Oct 6 after refusals from 05:17 through 13:45, which is consistent with a customer retrying for about 8 hours.
102	- Customer-visible effect is a generic failure in the wizard rather than "sold out" copy. Fix: surface a clear "this size is temporarily unavailable in region X, try Y" with a notify-me option; log the userId on refusals so they can be counted.
103	
104	### 7. Mid-session breakage after deploys and a handful of 5xx on customer paths (quick)
105	- "Failed to find Server Action" (stale client after a deploy) appeared 253 times, 231 on Oct 1 (deploy day); client errors "Loading chunk N failed" about 30 over two weeks; React `removeChild` errors in the dashboard 41 (typical of browser translation/extensions, 4 browsers), "An error occurred in the Server Components render" 27.
106	- nginx 5xx on real customer paths this week: /login 502 x29 on Oct 6 (crash window 15:23-15:28 UTC, 60 502s in the hour), x9 Oct 3, x6 Oct 1; /dashboard/servers/* 502 x48; /dashboard/support 500 x45 on Oct 4 16:xx; /api/chat/upload 500 x22 (Oct 1 14:xx). No 500 on /dashboard/deploy or /register in the week.
107	- Fix: serve a "new version available, refresh" prompt on server-action failure (the deploy wizard in particular); investigate Oct 4 /dashboard/support 500s and Oct 1 chat upload 500s.
108	
109	### 8. Hosting wizard validation dead-end and miscellaneous (quick)
110	- Hosting wizard: "Enter a valid domain (e.g. example.com)." fired twice on step Payment (Sept 26 and 27), i.e. the user got all the way to checkout before the domain was validated. Move validation to the Domain step. Hosting accounts for 3 of 84 wizard users this week, so this is low priority.
111	- Verification: 8 of 31 email signups this week never verified (15 users overall across two weeks); 10 of those 15 used the deploy wizard anyway, so verification is not blocking them. The verification link redirected to https://0.0.0.0:3000 until the fix at Oct 5 02:26 UTC reached prod (Oct 5 10:50 release); users who clicked it before then saw a broken page. Email-verify opens 19 of 36 (53 percent); clicks are not tracked on verify links.
112	
113	## Win-back and other lifecycle emails
114	- deploy_winback: 121 distinct recipients in 14 days (69 this week); 17 opened (14 percent), 5 clicked (4 percent), 31 returned to the site, 5 ordered something afterwards and 2 topped up, 0 redeemed COMEBACK50. Marketing mail is working technically but is not moving revenue; the 50 percent offer is not the lever for this audience.
115	- server_deployed: 74 sent, 22 opened. invoice_new 107 sent, 15 opened (14 percent).
116	
117	## Notable individual cases (masked)
118	- Customer h***: Bedrock server failed at 19132/udp three times on Oct 6 morning (two nodes), asked in chat how to invite a Bedrock player; likely the NetherNet default bug fixed at 05:34. Worth a proactive "fixed, redeploy" note once ticket replies are approved (no replies sent by this analysis).
119	- Customer z***: Valheim at 2456/udp on node 178.63.94.114 failed three times Oct 1, then succeeded on the 8 GB plan; two 8 GB servers (Valheim, Project Zomboid, Oct 2) still show the "large download" step text 4.6 days on, no ready email.
120	- Customer f***: 27015 (Source-engine) game failed twice Oct 2 within 40 minutes, then retried; a real customer hitting repeated failures like this is the case worth a proactive follow-up.
121	- Customer c*** (Sept 4 signup): "PVE POST .../qemu/657/config -> 403 Permission check failed" at game provision, Oct 4: a Proxmox token-permission failure on a node (not a customer mistake); same family as the known split-token item.
122	- A new-user ticket "Server cannot be created" (Oct 1) and "VPS web-01 stuck in ERROR state" (Sep 28): both closed; one failed dedicated-IP purchase was refunded automatically on Sep 28 (255 cents).
123	- Admin impersonation produced a customer-style error "This action is disabled while impersonating" on Sept 26 inside the VPS wizard, which is expected behavior, not a customer problem.
124	
125	## Context for the Oct 5-6 changes

142	---
143	name: nxeon-worktree-nodemodules-hazard
144	description: "NEVER git add -A in a worktree that has a node_modules symlink — it can destroy prod's real node_modules"
145	metadata: 
146	  node_type: memory
147	  type: feedback
148	  originSessionId: 4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc
149	  modified: 2026-08-21T17:19:08.560Z
150	---
151	
152	On 2026-08-21 I nearly took prod down. In a worktree I created `node_modules` as a symlink to `/opt/nxeon/node_modules` (the standard setup), then ran `git add -A` which COMMITTED the symlink (`.gitignore` has `node_modules/` with a trailing slash, which does NOT match a symlink named `node_modules`). Fast-forwarding that commit into the prod tree `/opt/nxeon` replaced its **real** `node_modules` directory with a **self-referential symlink** (`/opt/nxeon/node_modules -> /opt/nxeon/node_modules`), deleting 1.1G of packages. `next` and the Prisma client became unresolvable; only the in-memory running services survived.
153	
154	**Why:** never stage the whole tree in a symlinked worktree.
155	**How to apply:**
156	- In worktrees, `git add` ONLY the specific files you changed — never `git add -A` / `git add .`.
157	- Recovery if it happens: `git rm --cached node_modules && rm -f node_modules` in the prod tree, then `npm ci` (lockfile present) + `npx prisma generate`, then commit the untracking. Do this BEFORE any restart/promote — running services hold modules in memory but a build/restart will fail hard.
158	- Consider hardening `.gitignore` with a bare `node_modules` line (no slash) so the symlink is ignored too.
159	
160	Relates to [[nxeon-build-isolation]] and the deploy flow in [[nxeon-resume-point]].

172	Never use phrasing like "our provider," "our infrastructure partner," "our network provider," or any language that implies Nxeon depends on a third party for its core infrastructure, in any customer-facing communication (support tickets, emails, UI copy, chat responses). Nxeon must always speak in its own voice as if it fully owns and operates its infrastructure — "our network," "our systems," "our DDoS protection," never "our provider's X."
173	
174	**Why:** On 2026-08-29, in a support-ticket reply about DDoS protection capacity, I wrote "Our provider's stated policy is explicit on this..." — the user corrected this immediately: "you should never mention to customer 'our Provider' or 'OVH' in their eyes, we don't have a provider, we are the provider. it devalues our company image." This is stricter than just "don't name the vendor" (already established in [[nxeon-multi-registrar-plan]]-adjacent work for hiding registrar identity) — even a generic, unnamed reference to "a provider" undermines the brand positioning that Nxeon owns its stack end-to-end. The correct phrasing was already used in the SAME thread's first reply ("Our network-level DDoS filtering operates...") — that's the model to follow.
175	
176	**How to apply:** Before sending any customer-facing text that describes infrastructure, security, or capacity, scan for "provider," "partner," "vendor," "upstream," or similar reseller-revealing language and rewrite in first-person-owner voice. This applies even when the underlying technical fact is genuinely sourced from a real hosting/network partner (e.g. OVH) — the vendor's name must never appear (established separately), AND the fact that a vendor exists at all must not be implied either. Research/verify real technical facts from the actual vendor's documentation as needed (that's still correct and necessary for accuracy — see the DDoS-capacity ticket work), but always present the resulting capability as Nxeon's own when relaying it to a customer.

196	=== nxeon-checkout-conversion-research
197	---
198	name: nxeon-checkout-conversion-research
199	description: What the checkout/conversion evidence actually says for the Nxeon deploy wizard — and which widely-quoted numbers are fabricated
200	metadata:
201	  type: reference
202	---
203	
204	Research done 2026-09-05 for the single-page deploy wizard. Sources are
205	Baymard, NN/g, peer-reviewed journals and the competitors' own live flows.
206	
207	**The premise "one page converts better" is not supported.** Baymard's position
208	is that page count is close to irrelevant — *"the number of form fields impacts
209	overall usability far more than the number of steps."* Average checkout is 11.3
210	fields; most sites need 8. So cut FIELDS, not pages.
211	
212	**The single highest-leverage move is pre-selected defaults.** DigitalOcean's
213	create page: *"The most popular defaults are pre-selected, so you can scroll to
214	the bottom of the page and create a Droplet immediately."* Johnson & Goldstein
215	(2003, Science) — opt-in→opt-out roughly doubled consent, 42%→82%. Only
216	non-committal defaults: nothing that adds to the total.
217	
218	**Top abandonment reasons** (Baymard, 70.22% avg across 50 studies):
219	extra costs 40% · card distrust 19% · forced account 18% · too long 17% ·
220	can't see total up-front 12%. So: show the true total INCLUDING the renewal
221	price before any payment field, and visually ENCAPSULATE the card fields — in
222	testing the container did the work, not which seal was used.
223	
224	**Pre-ticked paid add-ons are illegal in the EU.** CRD 2011/83/EU Art. 22: consent
225	inferred from a default the consumer must reject entitles them to
226	reimbursement. A pre-ticked backup is a chargeback generator. EU B2C must also
227	display VAT-INCLUSIVE prices wherever a selling price appears — relevant to the
228	open VAT decision.
229	
230	**Plan-table psychology:** centre-stage effect replicates (Valenzuela & Raghubir
231	2009 — inferred popularity, not attention). The DECOY effect does NOT (Frederick
232	et al. 2014; Yang & Lynn 2014) — do not build a decoy tier. Use ONE badge, not
233	two. Choice overload is conditional (Chernev 2015): it bites hardest under
234	preference uncertainty — exactly the game-server buyer who doesn't know what RAM
235	they need, which argues for a use-case selector that recommends a tier.
236	
237	**Numbers circulating online that are FABRICATED — never cite these:**
238	"Baymard found multi-step beats single-page in 67% of tested cases" and "a
239	15-field form across three steps beats a 10-field single page by 11-14%" are not
240	on Baymard's site at all. Also unverifiable: "most popular" badge +16-30%,
241	money-back guarantee +21%/+26%/+300%, Mailchimp +21% annual framing, Formstack's
242	"multi-step converts 3x" (correlational), Shopify one-page "+7.5%" (one store,
243	no A/B test).
244	
245	**Competitor split:** developer clouds (DigitalOcean, Hetzner, Vultr) configure
246	BEFORE commit with a live price and no guarantee — hourly billing is the risk
247	reversal. Retail hosts (Hostinger) sell a plan, then configure AFTER payment,
248	with 30 days money-back. Game hosts are tighter still: Shockbyte 72-hour
249	self-serve refund, GPORTAL a $1.42 3-day trial. Hetzner puts type/size BEFORE
250	location so the price anchor lands first.
251	
252	**Add-ons convert best post-purchase**, on the provisioning screen, where the
253	order is already banked and cannot be lost. Keep only spec-relevant ones inline.
254	
255	See [[nexion-ui-sandbox]], [[nxeon-hosting-wizard]], [[nxeon-deploy-winback]].

268	
269	**What shipped:** `Visit.ua` was already captured on every request — added 3 new nullable columns (`deviceType`, `os`, `browser`), parsed at ingest time in `app/api/track/route.ts` via a new `lib/ua-parse.ts` (`ua-parser-js@2.0.10`), and 3 new `topDeviceTypes`/`topOperatingSystems`/`topBrowsers` functions in `lib/analytics.ts` mirroring the existing `topCountries` groupBy pattern. Rendered as 3 new `<RankedList>` cards on `app/admin/visitors/page.tsx` (the real traffic dashboard — not `app/admin/analytics/page.tsx`, which is revenue-focused). Backfilled all 4,003 existing visits that already had a stored `ua` via `scripts/backfill-ua.ts`.
270	
271	**ua-parser-js v2 API note:** callable directly as `UAParser(ua)`, not `new UAParser(ua).getResult()` (that's the v1 API). `device.type` is `undefined` for ordinary desktop browsers — the library has no positive "desktop" signal by design — so `deviceType` defaults to `"Desktop"` when unset. Correctly disambiguates iPad (tablet+iOS) from Mac (no type+macOS).
272	
273	**Bug hit twice, same root cause:** `import "server-only"` in `lib/ua-parse.ts` broke any plain-`tsx` process that imports it — first the backfill script, later would have hit prod's `worker/index.ts` too if left in. Same class of bug as an earlier session's `lib/google-ads.ts`/`lib/riddle.ts` worker crash (`server-only` has no valid entry point outside a bundler). Removed the import; documented why in the file. **Lesson: any new `lib/*.ts` file must NOT have `import "server-only"` if there's any chance a plain-tsx script (backfill, worker) will import it — check call sites, not just the primary intended caller.**
274	
275	**Deploy-tooling gotcha confirmed again:** `promote-production.sh`'s `npm install` step (even a no-op "up to date") can leave main's `node_modules/@prisma/client` stale relative to a `prisma generate` that was only run in a sibling worktree — even though `node_modules` is nominally shared/symlinked. Always re-run `npx prisma generate` (and `npx tsc --noEmit`) directly in `/opt/nxeon`'s own tree right before `promote-production.sh`, not just in the worktree, after any schema change.
276	
277	**Also hit:** a stale `next start` scratch-verification server from an earlier, already-deleted worktree (`nxeon-wt-stripfix`) was still squatting on port 3998, silently swallowing a "verify locally" curl test and making it look like the new fields weren't being written (they were — just not by the server I thought I was hitting). Confirmed via `ss -tlnp` + `/proc/<pid>/cwd` showing `(deleted)` before killing it. **Lesson: always verify which process actually owns a scratch port before trusting a "success" from `npm start &` — a background start can silently fail with EADDRINUSE while the shell shows no error.**
278

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
